faq.a: Rashidi is associated with the Arabic form رَشِيدِي, whose core sense is rashidi; rightly guided (swahili form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Rashidi?
faq.a: Rashidi is associated with Arabic. Rashidi is the Swahili form of Arabic رَشِيد (Rashīd), meaning 'rightly guided'.
Yes — the underlying form رَشِيدِي is Arabic.
Rashidi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Rashidi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Rashīd is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Rashidi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Rashidi is rendered رشیدی and carries the sense رشیدی، ہدایت یافتہ.

faq.q: What does Rashidi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Rashidi is rendered رشیدی and carries the sense رشیدی، هدایت‌یافته.
A romanized syllable approximation is ras-hi-di. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Rashidi?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Rashidi, rashidi. Script forms are رشيدي, رشیدی, رَشِيدِي, रशीदी.

faq.q: Is Rashidi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
